local_facts.title: A maintained Atlantic shoreline and a recorded wind event
local_facts.claim: Boca Raton says it manages more than 4.75 miles of shoreline. NOAA records that Hurricane Wilma caused widespread wind damage in Boca Raton on October 24, 2005, where the city remained in the eyewall longest.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Near-coast hardware merits a close corrosion check, and after major wind the tracks, struts, fasteners and attachment points need inspection even when the door still moves.

local_facts.title: Sectional and rollup doors are product-approval categories
local_facts.claim: Palm Beach County identifies sectional and rollup exterior doors as covered categories in Florida’s product-approval system. Florida’s hurricane retrofit guidance says an approved product carries installation requirements that vary with wind zone and exposure category.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A replacement is not only a panel choice. The selected model, size, track, fasteners and installation details have to match the opening and its approved configuration.

local_facts.title: An exterior replacement can have an HOA step
local_facts.claim: Boca Raton’s HOA affidavit says a City permit does not exempt an owner from HOA regulations. Southwind Lakes’ local architectural-review form specifically requires HOA approval before replacement garage-door work starts.
local_facts.why_it_matters: For an HOA property, confirm the association’s required panel style, color, windows and approval process before ordering a street-facing replacement door.
